sections.title: Which floor?
sections.content: You already know emelet ("floor, storey") and the ordinal numbers első, második, harmadik. Put them together with the -on/-en/-ön ending you already use for locations, and you can say and ask which floor a room is on: a harmadik emeleten ("on the third floor"). The question word is hányadik — "which one, in order?" — so hányadik emeleten? asks "on which floor?"

sections.title: Which floor
rows: What floor is my room on?

items.spanish: A szoba a harmadik emeleten van.
items.english: The room is on the third floor.
What floor is my room on?

sections.content: hányadik ('which one in the sequence') is different from hány ('how many') — you're already using hány for quantities like hány éjszakára; hányadik is for position in an order, exactly like an ordinal number answers it.
